text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A Sunday Times investigation shows that soaring costs of hospital treatment is driving Nigerians to quacks when they take ill.
- Organisation of African Unity donates $200,000 to the Economic Community of West African States in support of its efforts to restore peace in Liberia.
- Persistent fuel scarcity takes it toll on food prices as retail costs of major staples begin to rise.
- Nigeria qualifies for next year's World Cup tournament in France after thrashing Kenya 3-0 in Lagos on Saturday.
- Baptist, Catholic and Methodist churches have applied to the education ministry to allow them set up private universities in Nigeria.
- Pastor Alexander Baba, supreme head of Celestial Church of Christ returned to Lagos at the weekend after a two-month trip to Europe and dispelled speculation about his health.
- The crisis in Sierra Leone may degenerate into a regional conflict as Libya, Ivory Coast and Burkina Faso back the soldiers who seized power there in a coup two weeks ago.
- Foreign partners in the Nigerian liquefied natural gas (LNG) project seek audience with oil minister Dan Etete over dissolution of board of directors of the LNG company.
- Security beefed up at Lagos international airport in an apparent alert over recent bomb blasts in Nigeria.
